key_insight: The paper formulates a turbulence closure where the displacement-volatility field is solved jointly with velocity using Itô–Hencky kinematics, rather than prescribing covariance or eddy viscosity.
engineering_relevance: This creates a mechanically consistent stochastic closure framework that can support more faithful uncertainty-aware CFD, especially when momentum-source covariation and boundary effects matter.
method: One-channel Itô configuration map with local matrix-logarithm expansion
Derives material and spatial Hencky increments plus exact pathwise volume constraint
Builds an index-one velocity–volatility–pressure DAE with virtual-power-consistent stress impulse
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical derivations and limiting-case consistency results, plus a Green–Kubo realization for finite-correlation covariance, but no numerical benchmark data.
watch_item: The framework appears mathematically intricate and may require careful treatment of boundary reactions, covariance compatibility, and DAE stability in implementations.
paper_title: Foundations of a solved-volatility stochastic turbulence closure: Itô--Hencky kinematics, source-consistent momentum and finite-correlation realisation
